edges.label: Snowball Chamber co-developers; the dark-matter group whose instrumentation was carried into the UAP field work
edges.note: Levy's faculty page lists 'Szydagis, Knight, Levy, The Snowball chamber: neutron induced nucleation in supercooled water' (arXiv:1807.09253, 2018) and describes the Snowball Chamber as 'a research topic completely unique to the UAlbany dark matter group'. The UAlbany release makes the methodological carry-over explicit: the C-TAP frame-differencing software is 'similar to an approach used by physicists like him and Levy to look for direct evidence of dark matter'. This is the mechanism by which rare-event detection practice reached UAP field work at this institution.

edges.label: Employs Levy; Associate Professor of Physics and the third UAlbany author on the 2025 UAPx paper
edges.note: Levy is an LZ dark-matter physicist in the same department and co-developer, with Szydagis, of the Snowball Chamber supercooled-water detector. The University's own news office names her as one of three 'UAlbany authors' on the 2025 Progress in Aerospace Sciences field-expedition paper. Her faculty page does not itself list UAP among her research interests, which is worth recording rather than smoothing over: unlike Szydagis, her UAP involvement appears in the publication record and the university press office but not in her stated departmental research profile.
